read: partial: main text pp.1-10 and appendix A.1-A.7 (pp.14-27) read; the model-output figures (pp.18-23) skimmed. The file is the ICML 2025 version (arXiv 2508.08292v2), not the NeurIPS 2024 workshop version the May paper cites
venue_now: ICML 2025, PMLR 267 (p.1); arXiv 2508.08292v2, 27 Aug 2025. The May reference (L992) cites the 4th Workshop on Mathematical Reasoning and AI at NeurIPS 2024
what_it_is: Putnam-AXIOM is 522 problems from the William Lowell Putnam competition (1938-2023) across 11 university-level domains, chosen for a unique final answer; 221 of them (42.3%) were modified with a 'trivial next step' so that proof-style problems end in a single boxed answer (p.1, p.4). A Variation set gives 100 problems Python scripts that change variable names (63) or also constants (37) and rephrase the statement, producing an unlimited supply of new instances (p.1, p.4-5). Answers are scored by exact match through a SymPy-based equivalence function (p.2, p.5, p.26), and Teacher-Forced Accuracy (TFA), the share of reference-solution tokens a model predicts under teacher forcing, is proposed as a cheap proxy for reasoning quality (p.5-6). o1-preview solves 41.94% of the originals (p.7), and most models score lower on the variants than on the matching originals (Table 2, p.14).
size: 522 original problems, 100 of them with functional variants (p.4); 18 models in Table 1 (p.7) and 21 in the variation comparison (Table 2, p.14)
source_of_items: competition (Putnam 1938-2023), partly modified to give boxed answers (p.4); variants generated by perturbing variables and constants with Python scripts (p.4-5)
instances: static originals plus generated (perturbed) variants for 100 problems; each evaluation uses five random snapshots (p.4-5)
has_gold_traces: partial: problems keep their written reference solutions (p.3-5), which TFA uses as the teacher-forced reference; they are not used to check a model's own steps
evaluation: final answer (boxed answer, SymPy-based equivalence; p.2, p.26) plus a proxy metric, teacher-forced accuracy against the reference solution, which needs access to log-probabilities (p.5-6, p.9, p.25)
human_validation: None reported for the problems, the modified boxing or the variants. The authors analysed model outputs qualitatively (p.7-8) and leave the comparison of TFA with expert grading to future work (p.9).
contamination_measures: perturbations: functional variants for 100 problems (p.4-5); in a LoRA fine-tuning test, accuracy on the trained originals rose from 23% to 80% but on their variants only from 12% to 33% (p.5)

engtrace_use.sentence: S-M1 (L155-161): In mathematics, benchmarks ranging from GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021) and Math (Hendrycks et al., 2021b) to HardMath (Fan et al., 2024), Putnam-Axiom (Gulati et al., 2024), and GSM-Symbolic (Mirzadeh et al., 2024) rigorously test abstract logical deduction and reasoning stability.
engtrace_use.explanation: The gist holds: Putnam-AXIOM is hard university-level competition mathematics, and its Variation set probes how stable performance is under perturbation, which matches 'reasoning stability' (p.4-5, p.14). But 'rigorously test abstract logical deduction' overstates what it checks: scoring is exact match of a boxed answer (p.5), 42.3% of the problems were rewritten to have one (p.4), and the authors write that final-answer accuracy 'cannot penalize lucky guesses on binary questions, detect spurious derivations, or compare the quality of two correct proofs' (p.5), and find o1-preview reaching correct answers through unjustified claims (p.7). The sentence also omits what matters most for EngTrace: programmatic variants for contamination resilience (p.1, p.4-5), a mechanism close to EngTrace's templates. The citation is to the 2024 workshop version; the text reviewed here is the ICML 2025 version.

suggested_wording: Putnam-AXIOM (Gulati et al., 2025) adds programmatically perturbed variants of 100 of its 522 Putnam problems, on which most models score lower than on the originals, but scores only the boxed final answer, proposing teacher-forced accuracy as a proxy for reasoning quality.
facts_to_cite: 522 problems from the Putnam competition, 1938-2023, across 11 domains (p.4)
221 problems (42.3%) were modified by adding a step so that they end in a single boxed answer (p.4)
Functional variants exist for 100 problems (19.2%): 63 change variables only, 37 change variables and constants, and statements are rephrased; the scripts generate unlimited snapshots (p.4-5)
Scoring compares the boxed final answer with the ground truth through a SymPy-based equivalence function (p.2, p.26)
o1-preview solves 219 of 522 originals (41.94%); most models score below 10% (p.7)

On the 100 varied problems, 18 of 21 models score lower on the variants than on the matching originals, e.g. o1-preview 43 against 51 and GPT-4o 22 against 30, means over five snapshots (Table 2, p.14)
LoRA fine-tuning on the originals raised accuracy on them from 23% to 80% but on their variants only from 12% to 33% (p.5)

TFA, the share of reference-solution tokens predicted under teacher forcing, correlates 0.52 with boxed accuracy on Putnam-AXIOM (0.62 without two outliers, p.9) and about 0.66 on MATH, above the ROSCOE metrics (p.8-9, p.14-15)
TFA needs log-probabilities, so it was not computed for proprietary models (p.7, p.9)
The authors state that final-answer accuracy cannot penalise lucky guesses or detect spurious derivations (p.5)
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: programmatic generation of fresh instances (variants that change variables and constants, p.4-5) to resist contamination, which is EngTrace's motivation for templates; written reference solutions; a deterministic symbolic answer check (p.26); an explicit argument that final-answer scores miss flawed reasoning (p.5). Lacks: engineering or physical content; generation for most items (100 of 522, p.9); step-level verification of the model's own reasoning (TFA scores prediction of the reference solution, cannot be computed for closed models and has not been compared with human judgement, p.6, p.9); expert validation of items, variants or evaluator.
notes: Version: the May entry (L992) cites the NeurIPS 2024 workshop paper with seven authors; the ICML 2025 version reviewed here adds Elyas Obbad and 'in LLMs' to the title (p.1). The revised reference should cite the ICML 2025 version (key Gulati et al., 2025), and facts from it may differ from the workshop version, which I could not read; hence medium confidence. The paper is internally inconsistent: the abstract says o1-preview's accuracy 'drops by 19.6% (46.8% relative decrease)' on the variations (p.1), section 4.1 says 17% (p.7), and Table 2 gives 51 to 43 out of 100 (p.14); Appendix A.4 speaks of 262 original and 60 variation questions (p.24) against 522 and 100 elsewhere. The revised text should not quote a drop figure, or should cite Table 2. The name is Putnam-AXIOM.
